correctness.summary: Find records at most ONE run per period value. After recording (or even just matching) the first occurrence of a given period, the unconditional 'break' at the end of the matched-branch exits the entire 'start' loop, so all later non-overlapping runs of the same period are silently dropped. A method named after Main-Lorentz is expected to enumerate all maximal repetitions, but it misses many.
correctness.triggeringInput: s={97,97,98,98} ("aabb"), n=4. Period 1 has two distinct runs: "aa" at start 0 (length 2) and "bb" at start 2 (length 2). Find returns count=1 with only {Start=0,Period=1,Length=2}; the "bb" run at Start=2 is never reported.
correctness.rootCause: The 'break;' on line 54 is inside the 'for (start ...)' loop and runs after the first match for the current period, terminating the start scan. The subsumption-check loop was clearly intended to dedup overlapping runs of the same period across many starts, but the break prevents those later starts from ever being examined.
correctness.suggestedFix: Remove the unconditional 'break;' (line 54) so the start loop continues scanning all positions for the current period; rely on the subsumption check (and/or advancing start past the found run) to avoid duplicate/overlapping reports. Optionally skip start forward to start+len-period after recording a run to avoid re-reporting the same maximal run from interior offsets.

perf.summary: The whole routine is O(n^2) per period (O(n^3) total in the worst case) plus an O(count) subsumption scan; the genuine Main-Lorentz algorithm finds all maximal repetitions in O(n log n).
perf.currentCost: Outer period loop O(n), inner start loop O(n), inner k-compare O(period), and an extra O(count) subsumption scan per found run. Worst case approaches O(n^3).
perf.proposedChange: Replace the brute-force scan with the actual Main-Lorentz divide-and-conquer using Z-function / prefix-function on prefix and reversed suffix to find runs crossing the midpoint, giving O(n log n). At minimum, replace the O(count) linear subsumption check with an indexing keyed by period.
perf.rationale: This file is named MainLorentz but implements brute force; the named algorithm is asymptotically far better and is the intended contract. Massive cycle reduction for large n.
perf.risk: Significant rewrite; must preserve the exact set/ordering of Run outputs the current code emits (it emits the first non-subsumed run per period via the `break`). The true algorithm enumerates maximal repetitions which may differ in count/representation — confirm the intended output contract before changing.

perf.summary: The extension loop computes `len % period` every iteration; since len starts at 2*period it equals len-period region and can be tracked with a running index instead of a modulo.
perf.currentCost: `s[start + len % period]` performs an integer division/modulo per extension step — div is ~20+ cycles and is on the hot extension path.
perf.proposedChange: Maintain a cyclic index `int m = period` (since at len==2*period, len%period==0... actually track `int m = (2*period) % period == 0`), incrementing m each step and resetting to 0 when m==period: `if (++m == period) m = 0;` then compare `s[start+len] == s[start+m]`.
perf.rationale: Replaces a hardware division with an increment-and-compare (branch predictable, ~1 cycle), removing the div from the inner extension loop.
perf.risk: Must seed m correctly: at len==2*period the index is len%period==0, so start m at 0 before the first compare. Strength reduction of % to a counter is exact for non-negative len.

perf.summary: `period * 2` and `2 * period` are recomputed in loop headers/bodies; minor invariant hoist.
perf.currentCost: `period * 2 <= n` in the outer header and `start + 2 * period <= n` plus `len = 2 * period` each recompute the doubling.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist `int twoP = period << 1;` once per outer iteration and reuse for the header bound, the inner start bound, and the initial len.
perf.rationale: Shift instead of multiply and a single CSE per period; trims a few ops from inner-loop bound checks.
perf.risk: None — period is positive, period<<1 == period*2 exactly with no overflow for valid n.
